newsitem.title: UK: UK farmers seen raising 1997 wheat, barley areas.
newsitem.headline: UK farmers seen raising 1997 wheat, barley areas.

text.p: British farmers are likely to sow increased areas to wheat and barley in 1997 as a result of the European Union reduction in set-aside cereals land, leading food and agriculture group Dalgety plc said on Thursday.

"According to our best estimates the land released by set-aside will lead to most farmers increasing their cereal plantings by a significant quantity," said Barry Barker, national seed business manager for Dalgety Agriculture.
Barker said the 1997 wheat area was likely to reach 2.1 million hectares, 170,000 hectares more than in 1996.
The area for winter barley would also increase by 60,000 hectares to 820,000 hectares, while that for spring barley would remain broadly unchanged at 510,000 hectares, he said.

"We believe that 65 percent of the farmed land released from set-aside will be put down to wheat and a further 25 percent will go down to barley." Barker saidthe area sown to oats was exepcted to recover to its 1995 harvest level of 110,000 hectares, after last year saw a slight decrease in the area of oats grown.
Dalgety Agriculture is the agribusiness arm of Dalgety plc.
